# GitHub Actions (CI workflows, action pins, Dependabot for actions) (tooling)

<!-- Generated by `stackfoundry pack render` from a researched pack. Each rule cites [key] = a source below.
     Disagree with a rule? Record the repo's way in the pack's repoConvention and re-render, so a refresh keeps
     your decision. -->

Applies to: cli, plugin. Versions in use: actions/checkout v7.0.1 (3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1) (.github/workflows/ci.yml jobs unit, validate); actions/setup-python v7.1.0 (6d4fd22b20465ccc0f7354476588e8df7c9ca0e0) (.github/workflows/ci.yml job unit); actions/setup-node v7.1.0 (949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1) (.github/workflows/ci.yml job validate); @anthropic-ai/claude-code 2.1.307 (.github/workflows/ci.yml job validate, step 'Install Claude Code CLI'); runners ubuntu-latest (Ubuntu 24.04), windows-latest (Windows Server 2025), macos-latest (macOS 26 arm64) (.github/workflows/ci.yml jobs unit (matrix.os), validate).

## Rules

- **Keep every `permissions:` block explicit and read-only unless a job needs a write scope; grant a write scope at job level for that job only, never at workflow level. Setting any scope sets every unlisted scope to none.** A broad GITHUB_TOKEN turns any compromised step (a malicious dependency's postinstall, an injected command) into a write to the repository; omitting a needed scope makes the job fail with 403 because unlisted scopes become none. Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml top-level permissions (contents: read). [gh-secure-use, gh-workflow-syntax, zizmor-audits]
  This repo: The repo sets `permissions: contents: read` once at workflow level; zizmor's excessive-permissions audit prefers `permissions: {}` at workflow level plus per-job grants. Both jobs only read, so follow the repo; move to per-job grants as soon as one job needs more.
- **Run code from pull requests only under `pull_request`, never under `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`; if a privileged trigger is ever needed (labelling, commenting), it must not check out or execute the PR's code, and must not set `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true` on actions/checkout.** pull_request_target and workflow_run run in the base repository's context with its token, secrets and caches; checking out fork code there is a 'pwn request' that can take over the repo. Under `pull_request` a fork gets a read-only token and no secrets. Since checkout v7 the action refuses fork checkout under these triggers unless the opt-in input is set. Since actions/checkout v7.0.0 (refusal of fork checkout by default). Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml on: pull_request. [gh-secure-use, gh-events, checkout-v7, checkout-action-yml, zizmor-audits]
- **Never put a `${{ }}` expression carrying event data (anything ending in title, body, message, head_ref, ref, label, name, email, default_branch, page_name) inside a `run:` script. Pass it through `env:` and reference it as a quoted shell variable ("$TITLE"), or pass it as an action input.** Expressions are substituted into the script text before the shell runs, so a crafted branch name or PR title breaks out of quoting and executes commands on the runner (recent advisories: command injection via branch names and issue titles). Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml: no run step uses an expression today; expressions appear only in concurrency, name, runs-on and with (not shell contexts). [gh-script-injection, gh-secure-use, zizmor-audits, gh-advisories]
- **Pin every action by full 40-character commit SHA with a `# vX.Y.Z` comment, take the SHA from the action's own repository (not a fork), and keep the same SHA for the same action in every job.** A tag or branch can be moved to malicious code; a SHA cannot without a SHA-1 collision. A SHA copied from a fork, or two jobs on different SHAs, defeats review of what actually runs. Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml jobs unit and validate (all three actions pinned; SHAs verified against the release tags on 2026-11-09). [gh-secure-use, checkout-releases, setup-python-releases, setup-node-releases]
- **Set `persist-credentials: false` on actions/checkout unless a later step runs authenticated git; when a step does need it, set `true` explicitly.** By default checkout leaves the token configured for git (since v6 in a file under $RUNNER_TEMP rather than .git/config) for the rest of the job, where any later step, including npm postinstall scripts, can read it. Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml jobs unit and validate (both checkouts use the default true). [checkout-action-yml, checkout-readme, zizmor-audits]
  This repo: The repo uses the default (credentials persisted). The token is read-only (contents: read) and fork PRs get a read-only token, so the exposure is low; recorded as a question rather than a defect.
- **Keep the Claude Code CLI version pinned exactly in the install step and bump it by hand: Dependabot's github-actions ecosystem does not see npm installs inside `run:`.** An unpinned CLI can change what `claude plugin validate --strict` accepts between two runs of the same commit; a forgotten pin silently drifts behind (2.1.307 pinned, 2.1.319 latest). Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml job validate, step 'Install Claude Code CLI'; .github/dependabot.yml (package-ecosystem: github-actions only). [npm-claude-latest, npm-claude-2-1-307, dependabot-actions]
- **Give every concurrency group a workflow-specific prefix and cancel in progress only for pull-request runs.** Group names are global across workflows and case-insensitive, so a bare `${{ github.ref }}` group lets one workflow cancel another; cancelling on main would leave main without a verdict. Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml concurrency (group ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress only for pull_request). [gh-workflow-syntax]
- **Never use self-hosted runners for this public repository's workflows.** Any user can open a PR whose code runs on the runner and persist on or pivot from that machine. Here: not used here yet (all jobs use GitHub-hosted runners). [gh-secure-use]

## Bug categories

| Category | Look for | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| `expression-injection-in-run` (blocker) | A `${{ github.event.* }}`, `github.head_ref`, `github.ref` or other attacker-controllable context interpolated directly in a `run:` block (or in a script input of an action such as github-script). | Arbitrary command execution on the runner with the job's token and secrets. [gh-script-injection, zizmor-audits] |
| `privileged-trigger-runs-pr-code` (blocker) | `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` or `issue_comment` triggers together with a checkout of the PR head, `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true`, or use of artifacts produced by a PR run. | Fork code runs with write token and secrets: repository takeover, secret exfiltration, cache poisoning of main. [gh-secure-use, gh-events, checkout-action-yml, zizmor-audits] |
| `unpinned-or-mismatched-action-ref` (confirm) | `uses:` with a tag or branch instead of a 40-char SHA; a SHA whose `# vX` comment does not match the tag it resolves to; the same action at different SHAs in different jobs; a SHA from a fork. | A moved tag silently runs new (possibly malicious) code; reviewers approve a version that is not the one that runs. [gh-secure-use] |
| `token-scope-widening` (confirm) | `write` scopes or `write-all` at workflow level, a removed `permissions:` block (falls back to repository default), or a new job that writes without a job-level grant. | Excess write access for every step; or a job that fails with 403 because unlisted scopes became none. [gh-workflow-syntax, gh-secure-use] |
| `persisted-credentials-exposed` (suggestion) | actions/checkout without `persist-credentials: false` followed by third-party code (npm/pip installs with lifecycle scripts) or an upload-artifact of the workspace. | The job token is readable by later steps or leaks in an artifact. [checkout-readme, zizmor-audits] |

## Wiring

- Dependabot's github-actions entry uses `directory: /` so it scans .github/workflows; the single `actions` group bumps all actions in one PR so the shared checkout SHA stays identical across jobs. Fails as: A different directory makes Dependabot miss the workflows; ungrouped PRs can leave jobs on different SHAs.. Here: .github/dependabot.yml updates[0] (directory /, groups.actions patterns *). [dependabot-actions, dependabot-options]
- The commands the CI jobs run match the 'Checks before calling a change done' list in .claude/CLAUDE.md. Fails as: Local checks and CI diverge, so a change is called done that CI rejects (or CI stops checking something the docs promise).. Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml jobs unit, validate; .claude/CLAUDE.md 'Checks before calling a change done'. [gh-workflow-syntax]

## Testing

A workflow change is proved only by the CI run it triggers on the pull request: check that every matrix leg ran and the expected jobs appear. Static audit of the YAML (security and syntax) is the cheap layer before that; the repo has none yet.

- Harness: .github/workflows/ci.yml (the workflow itself is the harness; no workflow linter in the repo)
- Run: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -v (what job unit runs)`; `sh plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh verify-plumbing plugins/stackfoundry`; `claude plugin validate --strict . && claude plugin validate --strict plugins/stackfoundry (what job validate runs)`
- Trap: `-latest` labels move to a new OS version over 1-2 months after an announcement (ubuntu-26.04 is already published); a green run can turn red with no repo change. Pin an OS version on the matrix leg if the Python 3.11 floor must stay reproducible.
- Trap: Matrix job order is not guaranteed; never make one leg depend on another's side effects.
- Trap: A fork PR from a first-time contributor may wait for maintainer approval before CI runs: a missing check is not a pass.
- Sources: [runner-images, gh-workflow-syntax, gh-events, zizmor-audits]

## Security

- Dependabot creates alerts only for actions referenced by a semantic version, not for SHA-pinned ones. With every action SHA-pinned, vulnerability awareness rests on Dependabot version updates (weekly) and on watching the advisory database; no advisory exists for actions/checkout, setup-python or setup-node as of 2026-11-09. Here: .github/dependabot.yml; .github/workflows/ci.yml. [gh-secure-use, gh-advisories]
- Workflow dependency lockfiles (.github/workflows/actions.lock, generated by `gh actions-lock`) pin actions and their transitive action dependencies and verify the source repository at run time; GitHub calls this stronger than SHA pinning and Dependabot regenerates entries. Status: public preview per GitHub's changelog of 2026-10-14; InfoQ (2026-11-06) reports GA on 2026-10-28, while the GitHub docs page read still does not state a status. Not adopted here. Here: not used here yet. [gh-lockfiles-concept, gh-lockfiles-howto, gh-lockfiles-changelog, infoq-lockfiles-ga]
- Dependabot applies a default 3-day cooldown to version updates (github-actions supports only `default-days`); raising it gives the ecosystem time to detect a compromised release before it reaches a PR here. Here: .github/dependabot.yml (no cooldown key: default 3 days). [dependabot-options]
- `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.307` runs the package's postinstall script (`node install.cjs`) in a job whose checkout persisted the token; keep the job's token read-only. Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml job validate. [npm-claude-2-1-307, checkout-readme]

## Not reached

- Official GA announcement of workflow lockfiles: not found on github.blog; the GA date (2026-10-28) rests on the InfoQ article (read), while GitHub's own changelog read says public preview.
- Default job timeout-minutes: the part of workflow-syntax read did not state it, so no timeout rule is given.
- Node runtime of setup-python/setup-node v7: their release notes do not state it (checkout v7 is node24 per action.yml).
- npmjs.com versions page returned 403; versions were read from registry.npmjs.org instead.
- Availability of Python 3.11 on ubuntu-26.04 images (relevant when ubuntu-latest migrates): not checked.
